idiom_name: for over IntoIterator, with Iterator adapters for transforming walks
implementation_notes: The enumeration message is for, which desugars to IntoIterator::into_iter() followed by repeated Iterator::next(); implementing IntoIterator for a type makes it walkable with the same syntax as the standard collections, and choosing &T / &mut T / T selects borrowing, mutable borrowing or consumption (iter(), iter_mut(), into_iter()). The transforming messages are Iterator's provided adapters - map/filter/flat_map/fold/scan - which are lazy until a terminal adapter or the for loop consumes them, and enumerate()/zip() supply position-dependent or pairwise walks. A hand-written index loop over a Vec is a smell except where the algorithm needs the cursor or several collections by position.
pitfalls: The borrow checker refuses to mutate a collection while an iterator over it is alive - the runtime trap of other languages becomes a compile error, but removal still needs restructure (retain/drain, or collecting what to delete first).
Adapters are lazy and single-pass: a chain that is never consumed does nothing, and reusing a partially consumed iterator (or a &mut iterator) silently continues where it stopped.

for takes the collection by value when given an owned collection, moving it; iterate over &c or c.iter() when the collection must remain usable, and remember that into_iter() on an owned value transfers ownership of the elements.
